name: Idaho mine (Rocky Bar, last lot 1874)
quote: The mine has always borne a high revutation and has yielded large amounts of very good ore, but the vein on most of the levels has been stoped, and the oresent workings are in poor ore. The last lot of 13 tons yielded $97.50 per ton.

name: Vishnu mine (12-stamp mill run, c. 1881)
quote: A 12~stamp mill has been running on the Vishm ore for the oast three years. One run of 98 tons yielded $200 per ton, and for months at & time the mill produced from $35,000 to $45,000 per month.

name: Vishnu mine (shaft sulphide ore, 250-500 ft levels)
quote: Small bodies of sulphide ore, principally above the 500 foot level, are reported to have been mined, which ranged in value from $7 to $16 per ton in gold and silver. The average recovery by amalgamation is given as $2.65 per ton,

name: Wide West mine (Red Warrior, company mill average)
quote: In Red Yarrior district, the Wide Vest mine has been worked to a depth of 300 feet. The vein has averaged 2 feet in width and the ore has averaged in the 10-stamp mill, owned by the company, $35 per ton.

tonnage: production of $1,250,000 locally accredited to the Wide West; ore treated in 20-stamp mill on Red Warrior Creek
name: Wide West mine (Red Warrior, Raymond 1870 milling return)
quote: According to Raymond (1870) the vein was from 2 to 5 feet wide, wall defined, and gave a milling return of $40 per ton.

name: Red Horse prospect (Bear Creek, 1922 shipment)

name: E. N. Stone property (Keystone, dump grab sample)

tonnage: total production per U.S. Mint records slightly over $750,000; 10-stamp mill built 1903, ran intermittently 14 years
name: Franklin mine (mill heads, 1903-1917)
quote: From records, the mill heads averaged $27 per ton in gold and silver, the former predominating in value.

name: Franklin mine (oxidized ore, lowest drift)
quote: Oxidation is reported in evidence here and there in the lowest Franklin drift to a depth of about 450 feet beneath the surface. At such places, small amounts of ore were mined which assayed from $35 to $76 per ton in gold. Ore of this character and value was far more abundant throughout the upper levels where oxidation was more complete.

tonnage: 5-ton shipment milled at Rocky Bar; later ore hauled to Franklin mill yielded $45,000 gross
name: Verdun group (5-ton mill shipment)
quote: One 5 ton shipment sent to Rocky Bar for treatment "milled" $23 per ton, indicating a probable gross value of $40 per ton for the ore. Subsequent treatment at the nearby Franklin mill, to which the ore was hauled by team, yielded $45,000 gross.

name: Verdun group (4-inch vein sample, 1925)
quote: 4 sample was taken across a 4 inch vein in the third from lowest adit tunnel on the southeast claim of the group, near the point where the adit first exposed the vein. The ore shows considerable amounts of iron and manganese oxides. The sample assayed 1.66 ounces gold: 3,5 ounces silver; 1,8 percent lead, and no zinc,
